name: Nav Dasa (patient platform of Dasa S.A., Brazil's largest diagnostics group)
category: Laboratory diagnostics conglomerate + patient-facing digital health platform (results delivery, scheduling, telemedicine); AI is internal/lab-facing, not a patient interpreter
country: Brazil (national footprint, 59+ diagnostic and hospital brands)
stage: Public company (B3: DASA3), mature incumbent in turnaround — 2025 consolidated gross revenue R$12.247B (-27% due to hospital deconsolidation into Rede Americas JV with Amil, Apr 2025); Q4'25 net loss R$948M; diagnostics segment growing (+9.6% national diagnostics revenue in 2025)
pricing_model: Nav app free (results/scheduling). Pay-per-service: private exams and 24h online telemedicine consults (exact consult price only shown in-app [uncertain]); health-plan users covered by insurer. Subscription: Cartao Dasa +Saude discount card — Basico R$39.90/month, Plus R$59.90/month, discounts up to 60% on exams/consultations/surgeries/vaccines for holder AND dependents. No charge for viewing or interpreting results.
target_user: Mass-market patients of Dasa-brand labs (lay patients), families with dependents; physicians use separate professional side (89k doctors connected). B2B2C via health plans and the GoHealth scheduling app for hospitals.
scale_metrics: Durable threat by scale, not by product depth: 23M+ people served annually across the network; 250k+ partner physicians; 50k+ employees; Nav claims 12M users [uncertain — figure/date from Dasa blog]; 1M+ Google Play downloads, 4.3 stars / 17.6K reviews (solid for a lab app); results natively flow from 24 Dasa brands. Revenue is diagnostics volume, not software — Nav is a funnel, so its 'threat' is distribution reach, not interpretation capability.
core_features: Exam results viewing/downloading/sharing (single-exam report, consolidated daily report, full history); scheduling of exams and vaccines across 24 Dasa brands with OCR of prescription photos; 24h telemedicine (scheduled or immediate); remote check-in; prescription photo auto-reading (~700k readings, 97% under 15s, +10% conversion); dependents registration ('Minha Familia', incl. minors); reminders; home collection (coleta domiciliar) expanding in 2025; WhatsApp cited as a results delivery channel [uncertain]
signature_differentiator: Vertical integration nobody can copy: Brazil's largest lab network feeds results natively into one app across 24+ brands — zero upload friction, results appear automatically. On the back end, 30+ internal AI models (confirmed on Dasa's own blog) run the labs: NLP screening 6-10k reports/day for 43 diseases, deep-learning MRI denoising 40% faster, Med-PaLM 2 integration for complex reports (hepatic nodules), Entelai partnership for multiple sclerosis/Alzheimer detection, AI smart forms that spot screening gaps and suggest extra tests. Flagship closed loop: AI detects alteration -> notifies responsible physician -> breast cancer finding-to-treatment time cut from 17 to 7 days. Crucially, all AI faces the lab and the physician — the patient gets reports, not interpretation.
lab_data_handling: Native ingestion only: results auto-flow from Dasa-network LIS (24 brands) into the patient's history. NO external PDF upload, no non-Dasa lab ingestion, no manual entry — walled garden. Retest cadence is driven by physician orders (the OCR ordering loop makes reordering frictionless inside Dasa); no hardware play — no CGM, no wearables, no at-home chips, no annual blood panel product. Smart forms suggest additional tests at check-in.
family_dependents_depth: Basic: 'Minha Familha' lets a guardian register minors/dependents and view their results in one account; Dasa +Saude card discounts extend to dependents. Shallow beyond access: no pediatric reference-range UX, no caregiver mode with alerts, no hereditary-risk layer — even though Dasa Genomica sells hereditary predisposition tests, that stays a separate physician-oriented service never woven into a family risk view.
doctor_sharing: Share exam reports (PDF) with any physician from the app; 89k doctors connected on the professional side; in-app 24h telemedicine for immediate follow-up (Dasa's own doctors). No structured consult brief, no SOAP summary, no preparation layer for the patient's own doctor — sharing is a PDF hand-off.
action_loop_monetization: Classic lab action-loop: result in app -> free 24h telemedicine consult -> prescription -> photo the prescription (OCR) -> schedule next exam/vaccine inside Dasa -> discount card (R$39.90-59.90/month) locks the household in. Plus vaccine commerce, home collection, and B2B GoHealth scheduling (R$4.2M incremental revenue reported). Margin lives in diagnostics volume; interpretation is free because it IS the lab.
ai_approach: 30+ production AI models on Google Cloud (BigQuery, Dataproc, Vertex AI, Vision API OCR, Document AI; Gemini/Med-PaLM 2 for complex report support), built by #dasainova AI lab with collaboration with Center for Clinical Data Science / Harvard Medical School; Entelai partnership for neurodegeneration. Human-in-the-loop by design: AI flags, physician decides (image approval, anomaly notifications). Culture of published validation (e.g., Felipe Kitamura, ex-innovation director, neuroradiology AI researcher).
data_inputs: Own-network lab results and imaging (millions of records in one of the largest private healthcare data lakes in Brazil), prescription photos (OCR), insurance card images, call/feedback sentiment. No wearable, CGM, questionnaire-based, or patient-uploaded external data.
data_interoperability: Ingestion: native LIS from own labs + camera OCR (prescriptions, insurance cards). Exhaust: PDF download/share, print, WhatsApp delivery channel [uncertain]. No patient API, no FHIR, no Health Connect / Apple Health Records, no external-lab PDF import, no RNDS integration visible. The moat is one-directional: everything flows in from Dasa, almost nothing flows out.
platform: iOS + Android apps (br.com.nav), web at nav.dasa.com.br, separate Nav Pro app for professionals, Dasa Genomica portal for physicians.
onboarding: Register with CPF — if you ever did an exam at any of 24 Dasa brands, history is already there. Time-to-value near zero for the installed base (23M patients/year); for non-Dasa patients the app is mostly useless, which is the flip side.
data_visualization: Report-centric: results as lab reports (specific, daily consolidated, full), history timeline and a homepage claim of 'health evolution' view [uncertain — depth of any biomarker trend charts/scores unverified]. No scores, no reference-range overlay play, no consumer-style trends comparable to AI interpreters.
engagement_channel: Transactional by nature: push when result is ready, scheduling reminders, WhatsApp cited as channel [uncertain]. No community, streaks, education loop or proactive health cadence in-app (content lives in the web blog). Classic lab-app pattern: opens on the result, churns between events — the very pattern a continuous-interpretation product exploits.
clinical_validation_trust: Above-average credibility: internal AI operates with mandatory physician supervision; validation culture with published research (Kitamura/Dasa radiology studies) and named academic partners (Harvard CCDS); impact reported as hard operational metrics (17->7 days to breast-cancer treatment; 97% OCR <15s; MRI 40% faster; NLP reading 6-10k reports/day for 43 diseases). No patient-facing accuracy claims exist (nothing patient-facing to validate). Service reputation: Reclame Aqui 8.3/10 with 399 complaints, mostly app access/login failures — trust risk is operational reliability, not clinical.
regulatory_posture: Clean by construction: since the app delivers only reports and the AI supports physicians inside clinical workflows, patient-facing diagnostic claims never appear — SaMD exposure (ANVISA RDC 657/2022) sits with internal physician-supervised tools, and Dasa publicly stresses security/validation/regulation of medical AI. LGPD emphasized around its private health data lake. Pricing transparency is the weak spot: telemedicine price only visible inside the flow.
gaps_opportunities: GAPS (Dr. Exame openings): no patient-facing interpretation or AI education layer at all; walled to 24 Dasa brands — no external lab PDF upload (everyone with a non-Dasa exam is unserved); no biomarker trends/scores/biomarker timeline depth; no hereditary family-risk weaving despite owning Dasa Genomica; no retest cadence nudges beyond transactional reminders; telemedicine is generic, not result-anchored; no caregiver alerts. WORKS (inspiration): zero-friction native data capture; prescription-photo OCR making the order-to-schedule loop one tap; 30+ AI models aimed at closing finding-to-treatment time with the physician in the loop; dependents in one account; household-level discount subscription.
relevance: High — defines the category Dr. Exame must beat: Brazil's largest lab has distribution (23M patients/year) and deep AI, but its AI faces the lab, not the patient. Nav proves the transactional lab-app pattern (open on result, churn) and leaves patient-side interpretation, cross-lab ingestion, family risk and continuous engagement entirely open.
